# UDreamInputKeySelector

<!-- Generated by the DreamGUIReferenceDocs commandlet from reflection. Edit the header, not this page. -->

Inherits from [UDreamUIControl](DreamUIControl.md).

Declared in `Public/Controls/DreamInputKeySelector.h`.

A button whose label is a bound key, and which listens for the next one when clicked.

Two nodes and one behaviour, the button's anatomy exactly -- the face IS the root, with the key's
name centred on it -- because that is what this control is: a button carrying a value. Clicking it
ARMS it (bIsListening), the next key it is told about becomes the value, and it disarms.

WHERE THE KEY COMES FROM, plainly, because this plugin has no hook that would supply it and this
class does not pretend otherwise. What exists here is:
  - UDreamUIActionRouter, which routes NAMED actions from a data table. It resolves a key to an
    action and fires that action's callback; it cannot report the key itself, and a rebinder needs
    the key, not the meaning.
  - ADreamStandaloneInputEventSystemActor, which does hold real FKeys -- its AnyKey binding is
    where they arrive -- but forwards them straight into navigation and the router and broadcasts
    nothing. OnAnyKeyPressed is private and not virtual.
  - UDreamUserWidget's Blueprint surface, which is pointer, drag, focus and navigation. No keys.
(UUITextInput does capture raw keys, by spawning an actor with AutoReceiveInput and binding every
key on it. That is a text field's bargain -- one actor per active field, consuming what it binds --
and inventing a second copy of it inside a control is not something this class does quietly.)

So the arming, the state, the visual and the value live here, and the KEY IS FED IN: while this is
listening, the project's input layer calls NotifyKeyPressed with whatever the player pressed, and
it returns true when it took it. That layer is wherever the project already sees keys -- its
PlayerController, an Enhanced Input action, or a subclass of ADreamStandaloneInputEventSystemActor
overriding BindActionRouting (which is virtual for exactly this kind of extension). SetSelectedKey
writes the value with no listening involved, for a settings screen restoring saved bindings.

UMG parity is UInputKeySelector's core: SelectedChord (with SelectedKey as its bare-key spelling),
bIsListening, OnKeySelected, OnIsSelectingKey -- plus the library's OnValueChangedBP, because the
key is a value and `<->` binds against it.

    /Script/DreamGUI.DreamInputKeySelector JumpBinding {
        SelectedKey = (KeyName="SpaceBar")
        OnKeySelected -> HandleJumpRebound

## Events

| Event | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OnKeySelected` | `void DreamInputKeySelectorKeyEvent__DelegateSignature(FKey SelectedKey)` | Fired when a key is bound, from a listen or from SetSelectedKey. Carries the chord's KEY. |
| `OnChordSelected` | `void DreamInputKeySelectorChordEvent__DelegateSignature(FInputChord SelectedChord)` | The same moment, carrying the whole chord. Fires alongside OnKeySelected. |
| `OnIsListeningChanged` | `void DreamInputKeySelectorListeningEvent__DelegateSignature(bool bIsListening)` | Fired when the armed state moves, so a screen can dim the rest of itself while one is armed. |
| `OnValueChangedBP` | `void DreamInputKeySelectorKeyEvent__DelegateSignature(FKey SelectedKey)` | The `<->` convention: two-way bindings synthesize their reverse route against this exact name, so a value control carries it alongside its spoken events. Fires with them. |

Every Blueprint-facing member of the UMG class, and where it went. *adopt*: same name, same meaning. *map*: here under another name or on another type. *reject*: deliberately absent, with the reason.

| UMG | Member | Status | Here | Note |

| `UInputKeySelector` | `TextStyle` | map | `Style` | The label's colour and size are FDreamInputKeySelectorStyle::LabelColor and FontSize; this library does not split a control's look into a button style and a text style. |
| `UInputKeySelector` | `SelectedKey` | map | `SelectedChord` | UMG's SelectedKey IS an FInputChord, so the chord is the faithful mapping. This control also carries a bare-FKey SelectedKey as the compatibility spelling existing .dui authors, kept coherent through every writer. |

| `UInputKeySelector` | `KeySelectionText` | map | `ListeningText` | SetKeySelectionText carries the UMG name and forwards. Empty keeps the built-in words, so a project overrides the prompt without overriding the control. |

| `UInputKeySelector` | `bAllowGamepadKeys` | adopt | `bAllowGamepadKeys` | On by default, which is what the capture agent already did. Off, a pad key is neither bound nor CONSUMED -- it was meant for something else, and swallowing it would leave a controller doing nothing while a selector is armed. The escape keys are checked first, so the pad's B is still a way out. |
| `UInputKeySelector` | `EscapeKeys` | adopt | `EscapeKeys` | Seeded with Escape and the pad's B. Emptying it is legal and means the click is the only way out, which the header documents as a trap. |
| `UInputKeySelector` | `OnKeySelected` | map | `OnChordSelected` | UMG's carries an FInputChord, which is OnChordSelected here. This control also fires OnKeySelected with the bare key from the same moment, for a consumer that only cares which key. |
| `UInputKeySelector` | `OnIsSelectingKeyChanged` | map | `OnIsListeningChanged` | Carries the new state, where UMG's carries nothing -- a handler that dims the rest of the screen needs to know which way it went. |
| `UInputKeySelector` | `SetSelectedKey` | map | `SetSelectedChord` | UMG's takes an FInputChord. SetSelectedKey exists here too and takes a bare FKey, which CLEARS any modifiers: 'bind exactly this key' is what a caller of the key-shaped setter is saying. |
